q: Which problem-seeking process states horizontal and vertical requirements and includes a space program with ambiance and cost?
n: Architectural programming is a problem-seeking process. It states horizontal and vertical requirements and includes a space program with ambiance and cost. Source: Peña & Parshall, Problem Seeking; 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: The architect sizes and configures spaces for given activities. This is:
n: Space planning sizes and configures spaces for given activities. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: The architect chooses and develops the type, arrangement and proportioning of structural elements with safety, cost, function and aesthetics in mind. This is:
n: Structural conceptualization chooses and develops the type, arrangement and proportioning of structural elements with safety, cost, function and aesthetics in mind. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3.

q: Formulating site criteria and helping the client evaluate sites for a project is:
n: Site selection and analysis formulates site criteria and helps the client evaluate sites for the project. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: An analysis of the space requirements of the project based on organizational structure and functional set-up pinpoints linkages and interaction of spaces.
n: Architectural programming analyses space requirements from the organizational structure and functions, pinpointing linkages and interactions between spaces. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201; Peña & Parshall, Problem Seeking.

q: Best way to approach an architect during Pre-design services.
n: Pre-design services begin with a consultation between client and architect to define needs. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: In which step of selection does the architect explain how he'll translate the project's requirements?
n: In the interview the architect explains how he will translate the project's requirements into design. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (selection of the architect).

q: Drawing usually done in the early stage of design?
n: Preliminary sketches are drawn at the earliest stage of design. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: Asan Architect, what must be done in the early stage of engagement with the client?
o: Explain well the scope of work of an Architect
n: Early in an engagement the architect must explain clearly the scope of his services, so the client knows what he will receive. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the client).

q: An architect prepared feasibility studies and marketing posters for a friend's townhouse project. What services were these?
n: Feasibility studies and marketing materials are pre-design services. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: By comparative selection, the client selects the architect by __.
n: In comparative selection, the client evaluates and ranks competing architects on qualifications and proposals. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (selection of the architect); RA 9184 (consulting services).

q: What are drawings that describe the character of the project as to structural, mechanical, electrical, and all other essentials?
n: Engineering drawings describe the project's structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing and other engineering systems. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: Who pays a full-time construction supervisor if the owner requires one?
n: Full-time construction supervision is an additional service separate from periodic site visits, and the owner pays for it. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 204-A.

q: Which method of compensation is flexible and easy to apply relative to size and complexity?
o: Lump sum fee or fixed fee
n: A percentage of project construction cost is the most flexible method of compensation. The fee scales automatically with project size and complexity. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (methods of compensation).

q: What should a prospective home builder/owner first do before proceeding with his/her project?
n: A prospective owner should first select an architect, who then helps define the project, budget and site and coordinates the engineers. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201 (pre-design services).

q: What should an architect do first on meeting a prospective client?
o: Submit a professional brief and fee proposal
n: On meeting a prospective client, the architect first presents his professional qualifications and a fee proposal, before any design work. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202; PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: Which step comes first?
n: Signing the service agreement comes first. No design work should start without a written agreement. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202; PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: What stage of the process does the professional fee of the architect get approved by the owner?
o: During the submission of the concept design
After the submission of the schematic design
During the submission of the schematic design
Before the submission of the schematic design
n: The architect's fee is agreed and approved in the service agreement before schematic design is submitted. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: What stage of the process does the probable cost of the project get submitted to the owner?
o: During the submission of the schematic design
After the approval of the schematic design
n: With the schematic design submission the architect gives the owner a statement of the probable project construction cost. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (schematic design phase).

q: The "project proponent" is the:
n: The project proponent is the client or owner who proposes and funds the project. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (definitions); DENR EIA rules (proponent).

q: In small scale projects, Clerk-of-work are commonly referred to as the:
n: On small projects, the clerk of works, the owner's full-time site representative, often doubles as the construction manager. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 204-A and 208.

q: On a renovation project, what is the architect's first obligation?
n: On a renovation, the architect must first notify the previous architect of the building before taking on work on his design. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to colleagues).

q: An arbitration panel has one representative from each party. Who is the third member?
n: In a three-member arbitration panel, each party names one arbitrator and the third, the chair, is a neutral member chosen by both or by the institution. Source: RA 9285 (ADR Act); CIAC Rules (EO 1008).

q: What is the first phase of the architect's regular design services?
n: Project definition (pre-design) is the first phase of regular design services, before schematic design. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: In the final submitted construction cost to the owner, who prepares the Bill of Quantities (BOQ)?
n: In bidding, the contractor prepares the priced Bill of Quantities as its final cost proposal to the owner. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (bidding); RA 9184 IRR.

q: Who prepares the Bill of Materials (BOM)?
n: The architect prepares the Bill of Materials as part of the contract documents, for estimates and permit submission. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202; NBC IRR Sec. 302.

q: The architect's plans, models and perspectives are called:
n: The architect's drawings, models and perspectives are instruments of service. They remain his property even after the project is built. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: Which is NOT within the scope of architectural practice?
n: The scope of architectural practice includes building maintenance and administration, site analysis and feasibility and promotional studies. Public administration is outside it. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (scope of practice).

q: What must the architect do before submitting sketches to a client?
n: The architect must sign a service agreement with the client before submitting sketches or other design work. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: A major shopping mall project is being developed by a large commercial client. Due to the complexity and scale of the project, a foreign architect specializing in retail planning and development was engaged. What would be the likely scope of work for the foreign architect?
o: Schematic, design, design development, and construction documentation
n: Under RA 9266, a foreign architect may practise in the Philippines only through a temporary special permit, working with a Filipino architect-of-record who signs and seals the documents. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38 (temporary/special permits).

q: A foreign retail planning specialist is engaged on a big mall project. What is his legal role under RA 9266?
n: A foreign retail specialist engaged on a mall is a consulting architect. He needs a PRC temporary special permit and cannot sign and seal permit documents. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: With a foreign consultant on the retail design, what is the Filipino architect's role under RA 9266?
n: The Filipino architect is the architect-of-record, who signs and seals the documents and takes legal responsibility for them. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20 and 38.

q: When a foreign architect is involved in a large commercial project for their retail expertise, what would be the typical scope of work assigned to the Filipino architect?
n: With a foreign retail consultant on board, the Filipino architect usually handles construction documentation and code compliance, then signs and seals as architect-of-record. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: In the event of a structural failure due to faulty construction on the same project, who would bear civil liability under Philippine law?
n: Under Art. 1723 of the Civil Code, if a building collapses from defects in construction, the person in charge of construction (with the contractor) is liable for 15 years. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1723.

q: On that mall project, who is the academically qualified professional with recognized expertise in a specific branch of architecture?
n: An architect as consultant is an academically qualified professional with recognized expertise in a specific branch of architecture. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 209 (consulting services).

q: During which stage does the architect provide the owner with the probable Project Construction Cost (PCC)?
n: The architect provides the owner with the probable project construction cost at the schematic design stage. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.
